 Japan Changes Tax-Free Shopping Rules: Tourists Must Pay Tax Upfront
 By 
Iuliia Tore 
 / Oct 29, 2026 / 3 minutes of reading Table of Contents
 Toggle How Japan’s New Tax-Free Shopping System Works 
 Japan Tax Refunds Must Be Processed Before Baggage Check-In 
 Minimum Spending Requirement Remains ¥5,000 
 What Travelers Should Know Before Leaving Japan 
 Subscribe to our daily newsletter 
 Don't Miss A News 
 Japan will introduce major changes to tax-free shopping on November 1, 2026, ending the system that allows international tourists to purchase eligible goods without paying consumption tax at the checkout. Under the new rules, visitors will pay the full price, including tax, and receive a refund only after customs confirms that the purchases are being taken out of Japan.
 The change affects travelers shopping at participating tax-free stores across Japan, including popular retail destinations in Tokyo, Osaka and Kyoto. Visitors purchasing electronics, cosmetics, clothing, luxury goods and souvenirs will need to allow additional time for departure procedures at airports and seaports.
 Japan Customs has confirmed that travelers must complete the required customs procedure within 90 days of purchasing eligible goods. The process will take place before departure, with customs verification required before the retailer can refund the consumption tax.

 How Japan’s New Tax-Free Shopping System Works 
 Until October 31, eligible international visitors can purchase qualifying goods at tax-free shops without paying Japan’s consumption tax at the point of sale.
 From November 1, the refund method replaces this arrangement. Travelers must initially pay the tax-inclusive price and complete customs verification when leaving the country.
 The new process requires visitors to present their passport at a tax refund terminal at the departure airport or seaport.
 After scanning the passport, travelers will receive one of two results:
 Green: No physical inspection is required, and the customs confirmation procedure is complete.
 Red: The traveler must present the purchased items at a designated customs inspection area.
 Once the required verification is completed, the retailer can process the eligible consumption-tax refund.
 Japan Tax Refunds Must Be Processed Before Baggage Check-In 
 One of the most important changes concerns airport procedures. Travelers must have their eligible purchases available for inspection before checking in their luggage.
 Japan’s National Tourism Organization warns that passengers who have already checked their purchases into the aircraft hold may be unable to complete the required customs verification.
 At major international airports, including Narita, Haneda, Kansai, Chubu Centrair, Fukuoka, New Chitose and Naha, travelers can also begin the procedure through Visit Japan Web using designated airport Wi-Fi.
 The digital option does not remove the requirement for customs confirmation or a possible inspection.
 Minimum Spending Requirement Remains ¥5,000 
 Under the new system, qualifying purchases must total at least ¥5,000 before tax at the same store on the same day.
 Tourists must take the purchased goods out of Japan within 90 days. Items consumed or used up during the visit, including food and cosmetics, are not eligible for a refund.
 Special sealed packaging for consumable goods will no longer be required, although travelers must still retain the items for possible customs checks.
 Gold and platinum bullion, along with goods already exempt from consumption tax, remain excluded.
 What Travelers Should Know Before Leaving Japan 
 The new system will make airport departure planning particularly important for tourists making substantial shopping purchases.
 Travelers should retain receipts, keep eligible purchases accessible and complete the customs procedure at their final international departure point from Japan.
 Those connecting from domestic to international flights must complete the procedure at the airport where they leave Japan, rather than at their initial domestic departure airport.
 Japan’s authorities also warn that travelers who fail to allow sufficient time for the procedure may lose their refund eligibility. Airlines and customs authorities will not compensate passengers who miss flights because of insufficient time for tax-free shopping checks.
 For visitors planning shopping trips from November 1 onward, the key change is straightforward: the tax benefit remains available, but it will no longer be deducted automatically at the checkout.
